resources.title: What Shapes Teacher Agency? Teachers’ Perceptions of Interconnected Influences in Government Schools in Bihar, India
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: The talk examines the factors that shape teacher agency in government middle schools in Bihar, with a focus on how different influences act as enablers and constraints. It draws on a research study conducted with government middle school teachers and school leaders. The study uses data from card sorting, influence mapping, teacher interviews, and a modified Delphi process. The collected data have been analysed using both quantitative and qualitative analytical approaches.
resources.citation: Bhatt, S., Khanna, M., Nanda, M., Patel, J., & Nath, S. (2026, November 19–21). What shapes teacher agency? Teachers’ perceptions of interconnected influences in government schools in Bihar, India [Paper presentation]. 16th Annual International Conference of the Comparative Education Society of India, Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, India.

resources.title: Bounded Freedom: Teacher Agency, Contested Narratives, and an Enabling Environment in Government Schools in Bihar, India
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: This panel examines teacher agency in government schools in Bihar, drawing on a mixed-methods study with 79 surveyed teachers and 62 participants in participatory research across five districts, conducted with the Aga Khan Foundation's Schools2030 initiative in Bihar. Moving from how teachers use their agency to the stories that shape how teachers are perceived. The presentation also foregrounds the factors influencing teachers and how we can build enabling environments to foster teacher agency.
resources.citation: Khanna, M., Bhatt, S., Diksha, M., & Jha, M.(2026, November 21). Bounded freedom: Teacher agency, contested narratives, and an enabling environment in government schools in Bihar, India. 16th Annual International Conference of the Comparative Education Society of India, Aligarh Muslim University, Aligarh, India. https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1JNWBMbynq6WQw-i79_EHbH_HK4K86a_Y/edit?usp=share_link&ouid=113633189525719312323&rtpof=true&sd=true

resources.title: Creating an Enabling Environment for Teachers: Voices from the Ground conveyed through a Policy Brief
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: Presented as part of the symposium “Bounded Freedom: Teacher Agency, Contested Narratives, and an Enabling Environment in Government Schools in Bihar, India,” this presentation draws on research with government school teachers in Bihar to highlight the everyday realities, constraints, and factors shaping teacher agency. It discusses the need to move beyond viewing teachers as bureaucratic implementers and recognise them as skilled professionals with knowledge and judgement. Drawing on voices of teachers and other education stakeholders -- headteachers, civil society organisations working in the field of education, education officers, and academics, it presents recommendations for strengthening professional autonomy, formalising teacher-led spaces for professional learning and dialogue, and cultivating supportive and inclusive school environments. The presentation also highlights efforts to translate research findings into policy dialogue and collective action.
resources.citation: Khanna, M., Patel, J., Nanda, M., Jha, M., Diksha, M., Nath, S., & Bhatt, S. Creating an Enabling Environment for Teachers: Voices from the Ground conveyed through a Policy Brief [Paper presentation]. 16th Annual International Conference of the Comparative Education Society of India, Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, India. https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1JNWBMbynq6WQw-i79_EHbH_HK4K86a_Y/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=113633189525719312323&rtpof=true&sd=true

resources.title: Access Interrupted: Voices of Teachers with Disabilities within the Ethico-political Architecture of Indian education system
resources.description: The presentation draws on a study of 32 teachers with disabilities (15 women, 17 men) across ten states, working in mainstream and special schools. Using semi-structured interviews, photovoice, and audionotes, it shows how access is interrupted at every stage: before they access the profession, and when they are within the profession. It also highlights how teachers navigate the challenges when support fails, and implications of the study.

Comparative Education Society of India, Aligarh. https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/11g8yR767oqb8gfCKbhTCHdz7xHFGbQCJ/edit?usp=share_link&ouid=113633189525719312323&rtpof=true&sd=true

resources.title: Happiness from the Lens of Children
resources.description: This flipbook explores a simple question: what brings happiness to children? Drawing on a study with 54 students from six government schools in Delhi, it uses Photovoice, a method in which children were given child-friendly cameras and invited to capture moments that make them happy. Accompanied by the children’s own captions, the photographs offer glimpses into their thoughts, memories, and experiences. They capture a range of feelings, from nostalgia to a sense of belonging to their school, relationships, and wider society. Alongside the photographs, children’s drawings offer insights into how they understand and express ideas explored in their Happiness classes, including kindness, mindfulness, friendship, and gratitude. More than a collection of images, this flipbook offers a window into children’s inner worlds, bringing their experiences and perspectives to life in their own words.
resources.citation: Nanda, M., Patel, J., Nath, S., Ravindranath, S., Khanna, M., Jha, M., & Bhatnagar, A. (2026). Happiness from the Lens of Children. White Falcon Publishing.

resources.title: Building Enabling Environments for Teachers Video Recommendations for Teachers and Headteachers
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: f we want every child to have a good teacher, we must also ensure that every teacher has an enabling, supportive, and trusting environment to work in. This video shares key recommendations from our policy brief, “Building Enabling Environments for Teachers: Voices from the Ground”, based on research with government school teachers in Bihar and their experiences of teacher agency, and the conditions that influence it. The brief argues that improving children’s learning is not only about changing what happens in classrooms, but also about transforming the systems around teachers — so that schools become places where teachers have professional trust, collaboration, autonomy, dialogue, and the support they need to thrive.

resources.title: Building Enabling Environments for Teachers: Voices from the Ground
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: This policy brief, developed by the TIDE Foundation in collaboration with the Aga Khan Foundation under the Schools2030 programme, explores the importance of creating enabling environments that strengthen teachers’ professional agency, autonomy, and well-being. Drawing on a research study on teacher agency and a multistakeholder roundtable in Bihar, it highlights the everyday challenges teachers face and calls for a shift from viewing teachers as mere implementers of directives to recognising them as skilled, reflective professionals. It presents actionable recommendations for teachers, headteachers, civil society organisations, and education officers, focusing on strengthening professional autonomy, formalising teacher-led spaces for professional learning and dialogue, and cultivating supportive and inclusive school environments.

resources.citation: Patel, J. N., Nath, S., & Nanda, M. (2024, December 27). “Gussa Kamm Aata Hai” (I feel less angry): Exploring how happiness education can be a catalyst for change. Retrieved from osf.io/7cdfk

resources.title: Putting our ideas into action A sample for a new science textbook
resources.description: This resource presents a sample science textbook lesson that uses COVID-19 to teach both scientific concepts and social-emotional learning by emphasizing accurate information, public health, collaboration, and responsible decision-making. It demonstrates how science education can connect real-world issues with students' development of empathy, critical thinking, and civic responsibility.
resources.citation: NISSEM (2022). Controlling Covid-19 through information and public health. www.nissem.org/blog/putting-our-ideas-into-action/2196/

resources.title: Guidance Note on teacher wellbeing in emergency settings.
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: This guidance note provides insight on how to promote teachers mental health, build enabling environments, and elevate teachers voices in times of crisis.
resources.citation: D’ Angelo, S., Sule, R., Mansour, S., & Patel, J. (2022). Guidance Note on teacher wellbeing in emergency settings. Interagency Network for Education in Emergencies (INEE). www.inee.org/resources/guidance-note-teacher-wellbeing-emergency-settings

resources.title: GUIDANCE NOTE Teacher Wellbeing in Emergency Settings
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: This Guidance Note gives you advice on how to support teacher wellbeing in the five domains of INEE’s (2010) Minimum Standards. It explains how to: promote mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) for teachers; create more enabling work environments for teachers; and enhance teacher voice, agency, and leadership in crises. ​We also offer you resources and tools and examples of these standards in action.
resources.citation: D’ Angelo, S., Sule, R., Mansour, S., & Patel, J. (2022). Guidance Note on teacher wellbeing in emergency settings. Interagency Network for Education in Emergencies (INEE). www.inee.org/resources/guidance-note-teacher-wellbeing-emergency-settings

resources.title: The role of dissent, conflict, and open dialogue in learning to live together harmoniously
fields: Teacher agency, wellbeing, motivation, and professional development
resources.description: Conflict, disagreement, and dissent are not obstacles to harmony but essential parts of learning to live together in diverse societies. The article emphasizes the importance of open dialogue, critical reflection, and respectful engagement with differing perspectives, suggesting that education should help students navigate conflict constructively rather than avoid it.
resources.citation: Patel, J. (2021). Dissent, conflict and open dialogue in learning to live together harmoniously. Educational Philosophy and Theory 55(6), 707-718. www.doi.org/10.1080/00131857.2021.2006057

resources.title: Citizens in the making; Inside the schools that prioritize 'harmonious living'.
resources.description: This article explores schools in India that prioritize harmonious living by fostering compassion, dialogue, community, and holistic approaches to developing responsible citizens.
resources.citation: ⁠Faculty of Education, University of Cambridge. (2021). Citizens in the making: Insights into schools that prioritise ‘harmonious living’. University of Cambridge.https://news.educ.cam.ac.uk/citizens-in-the-making-harmonious-living

resources.title: Learning to Live Together Harmoniously: a conceptual framework
resources.description: This article develops a conceptual framework for learning to live together harmoniously, arguing that education should help individuals cultivate peaceful relationships with themselves, others, and the wider world.
resources.citation: Patel, J. (2021). Learning to live together harmoniously; a conceptual framework. Cambridge Journal of Education 52(3), 327–347. www.doi.org/10.1080/0305764X.2021.1993791
